what: EPR Properties is a real estate investment trust that owns experiential properties: movie theatres, entertainment centres such as Topgolf venues, ski resorts, water parks, attractions and fitness centres, mostly leased to operators on long-term contracts.
customers: Operators of cinemas, golf entertainment venues, ski resorts and attractions, such as AMC, Regal and Topgolf, who rent its properties.
money: Theatres, Topgolf, ski resorts, attractions and fitness centres.
Early-childhood education properties being sold down.
moat: Long leases on properties that are hard to replicate, and expertise in a niche other REITs avoid.
risks: Cinemas are still a large part of the portfolio, and several tenants went bankrupt after the pandemic.
The GAAP P/E is not useful for a REIT because of depreciation; funds from operations is the right measure.
Free cash flow was negative over the last twelve months because of new investments.
opportunities: The dividend yields about 6.3% and is paid monthly.
The company is reducing its reliance on cinemas by investing in other experiences.
Eleven analysts average a target near $65, about 10% above the price.
Spending on experiences has held up better than spending on goods.
watch: Rent coverage at its theatre tenants and the pace of diversification.
view: For a REIT, earnings per share and P/E mislead, because depreciation of the buildings is a large non-cash cost. EPR’s funds from operations cover its 6.3% dividend comfortably, which is what income investors should care about.

The discount to other net-lease REITs exists because of cinemas. Theatres still make up a large part of EPR’s rent, and the industry has not recovered its pre-pandemic attendance. EPR has handled this sensibly, restructuring leases and shifting new money to Topgolf venues, ski resorts and attractions.

This turns on the theatres. If box office holds at today’s levels, the rent is safe and the yield is attractive. I think it is a reasonable income investment for someone who accepts that one of its main tenant industries will not grow.
bull: Box office stabilises, diversification lowers risk and the 6% yield is safe.
bear: Another wave of theatre bankruptcies forces rent cuts and a dividend reduction.
